reader_summary.headline: Hi and welcome to the A16Z podcast.
reader_summary.overview: Hi and welcome to the A16Z podcast. In this episode, we take a deep dive into the world of drug development, specifically undruggable drugs. Jay Bradner, president of the Novartis Institute for Biomedical Research, shares with A16Z general partners Jorge Condé and Vijay and myself all the new tools, technologies.

key_points.text: In this episode, we take a deep dive into the world of drug development, specifically undruggable drugs.
key_points.evidence_quote: In this episode, we take a deep dive into the world of drug development, specifically undruggable drugs, which is a category of protein or protein family or even a piece of RNA that's so difficult to target many researchers don't even want to touch it.

key_points.text: Jay Bradner, president of the Novartis Institute for Biomedical Research.
key_points.evidence_quote: Jay Bradner, president of the Novartis Institute for Biomedical Research, shares with A16Z general partners Jorge Condé and Vijay and myself all the new tools, technologies, and breakthroughs, which are the science of therapeutics to explode in some of these areas where it's been incredibly difficult or even impossible in the past.

key_points.text: From molecular glues to cell and gene therapies.
key_points.evidence_quote: From molecular glues to cell and gene therapies, Bradner shares the behind-the-scenes science stories of what it really takes to make a new drug that shatters the category of an undruggable target.

key_points.text: So I thought maybe we could start about just talking about what the category of undruggable really means to the industry.
